# Code Review Report

## Review Summary

This branch adds a new async OpenAI-compatible provider, unit and live integration coverage, and supporting documentation for the Python-native migration path. The implementation is close, but there are still a few contract mismatches between the new provider, the existing `ModelConfig` validation rules, and the documented configuration surface, plus one reliability gap in the new live test.

**Files Reviewed:** 7  
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 3 Warning, 1 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

None.

### Warning Findings

[W-01] Async provider advertises a provider key the runtime config cannot express
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/infrastructure/providers/openai_async_provider.py
Lines: 344
Description: `OpenAIAsyncProvider.get_supported_providers()` returns `"openai_async"`, but the current `ModelConfig` validation only accepts `openai_compatible`, and the new docs/tests instantiate the async provider with `provider="openai_compatible"`. That leaves the provider contract internally inconsistent: any future selection logic that matches `ModelConfig.provider` against `get_supported_providers()` will not be able to choose this implementation.
Suggestion: Make the provider identity consistent end-to-end. Either return `"openai_compatible"` here (or include it as an alias), or extend the configuration/selection layer so `openai_async` is a real supported provider key everywhere.

[W-02] JSON generation no longer gets the deterministic default used by the existing provider
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/infrastructure/providers/openai_async_provider.py
Lines: 147-149
Description: When `format_type == "json"`, the async provider sets `response_format={"type": "json_object"}` but still falls through to `temperature=0.7` by default. The existing synchronous provider explicitly defaults JSON generation to `temperature=0` when the caller does not override it. This async version therefore makes malformed or schema-drifting JSON more likely and breaks behavioural parity with the current provider family.
Suggestion: Mirror the synchronous provider logic: when `format_type == "json"` and no temperature was supplied, set `temperature = 0` before applying the general text-generation defaults.

[W-03] New live integration test bypasses the suite's existing availability skip guard
Category: Testing
Severity: Warning
File: tests/integration/test_openai_async_provider_live.py
Lines: 33-44
Description: The new test is marked `integration`, but it does not use the existing `llm_available` fixture from `tests/integration/conftest.py`. That fixture is the suite's standard way to skip cleanly when no live LLM endpoint is running. As documented in this PR, the new test hard-fails instead of skipping if the endpoint is down or the chosen model is unavailable, which makes ad hoc integration runs more brittle than the rest of the suite.
Suggestion: Accept the `llm_available` fixture in the test and use its returned base URL for the live call. That preserves the smoke-test intent while matching the rest of the integration suite's skip behaviour.

[W-04] README claims provider keys that current validation still rejects
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: docs/README.md
Lines: 29
Description: The updated README says the supported provider keys are `openai_compatible`, `ollama`, `lm_studio`, and `llama_cpp`, but the current `ModelConfig` validation only accepts `openai_compatible`. Users following this README guidance will hit a `ValidationError` instead of a working configuration. This also conflicts with the new async provider feature doc, which still uses `provider="openai_compatible"`.
Suggestion: Narrow the README claim to the keys that are actually accepted today, or update the config parsing/validation layer so those aliases are genuinely supported at runtime.

### Suggestions

[S-01] Unit tests bypass the constructor path they most need to protect
Category: Testing
Severity: Suggestion
File: tests/unit/test_openai_async_provider.py
Lines: general
Description: The new unit suite uses `__new__` construction plus patched internals throughout. That keeps the tests fast, but it also means they do not verify the real constructor path that normalises `base_url`, resolves the API key fallback, creates the initial `AsyncOpenAI` client, and seeds the per-host client cache. The live test gives some end-to-end coverage, but there is still no fast regression test for the provider's actual initialization contract.
Suggestion: Add at least one normal-construction unit test with `AsyncOpenAI` patched/mocked so the suite verifies `base_url` normalization, API key fallback, and `_clients` initialization without making network calls.

## Overall Assessment

This branch is directionally good and the scope is focused, but I would not merge it yet. The main risk is contract drift: the async provider, the configuration model, and the docs do not currently describe the same provider identity, and the JSON path has lost a reliability guard that the existing provider already uses. Once those mismatches are resolved and the live test adopts the standard integration skip gate, the feature should be in much better shape.
